previous_assumption: No notification system existed; assumed adding one would need a new permission code and/or realtime infrastructure (WebSocket/SSE/Redis).
correction: Built a minimal in-app notification module (apps/api/src/modules/notification, migration 0016) reusing the existing, previously-unused `organization.manage` permission (both org types already hold it) instead of adding a new permission code — notifications are organization-scoped (matches every other table's tenant pattern), not per-user, since every org today has exactly one member. Realtime is short-interval polling (apps/web/lib/use-interval.ts, ~4s for a live auction, ~25s for the notification bell) re-calling the same authoritative REST endpoints — NOT SSE/WebSockets/Redis. This was confirmed as the already-intended MVP approach, not just an inference: docs/marketplace-core-loop-design.md §8 explicitly says "the frontend polls" and docs/autonomus-building-instructions.md §14 explicitly sanctions this. Notification-trigger detection for auction started/ended lives at the SERVICE layer (AuctionService.notifyOnTransition, compares before/after status around syncStatus/closeNow calls) — deliberately NEVER inside AuctionRepository, confirmed by checking all 19 repository classes in this codebase: every single one takes only Kysely<Database> in its constructor, zero cross-repository or repository-to-service dependencies exist anywhere; adding one to satisfy notifications would have been the first such violation.
